passages.title: The Sugar Bush
passages.text: Every March, when the days turned warm but the nights still bit with frost, Grandpa Élie walked the maple trees behind his farmhouse with a hand drill. "The sap only runs when it thaws by day and freezes by night," he told Mireille, tapping a spile into the bark. She held the bucket steady while the first clear drops fell, slow as a leaking tap. It took forty litres of that watery sap to make just one litre of syrup, boiled for hours in the sugar shack until it thickened into gold. Mireille used to think maple syrup came from a bottle at the grocery store. Now, with sore arms and sap-sticky mittens, she understood why her grandfather called it liquid patience.

passages.title: The Last Streetlight
passages.text: Number seven was the only streetlight left standing on Larkin Avenue after the storm, and it flickered like it wasn't sure it should bother. Beneath it, three kids from the blackout block had dragged out lawn chairs, a deck of cards, and a flashlight for backup. "Lowest card loses a life," said Priya, dealing. Overhead, without the usual orange haze drowning them out, more stars showed than any of them had ever counted. Devon forgot to look at his hand entirely. "You can actually see the Milky Way," he said. Priya glanced up, then back down at her cards, unimpressed. "Play a card, or the Milky Way loses you your turn."

questions.prompt: What is this passage mostly about?
choices: A grocery store that sells maple syrup
A girl learning how maple syrup is actually made
questions.explanation: The passage follows Mireille learning, through the tapping and boiling process, how much work goes into making maple syrup.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how much sap does it take to make one litre of syrup?
questions.explanation: The passage states it took forty litres of sap to make one litre of syrup.

questions.prompt: Why does Grandpa Élie call maple syrup "liquid patience"?
choices: Because it tastes better with age
Because making it takes a long, slow process
questions.explanation: The slow drip of sap and the hours of boiling described in the passage are what he means by "liquid patience".

questions.prompt: In the passage, the word "thaws" most nearly means:
questions.explanation: "Thaws by day and freezes by night" contrasts warming with freezing, so "thaws" means to melt or warm up.

questions.prompt: What is the author's main purpose in this passage?
choices: To argue that store-bought syrup is better
To tell a small story about a change in understanding
To compare Quebec and Ontario farms
questions.explanation: The passage is a short narrative about Mireille's understanding of syrup-making changing, not an argument or instructions.

questions.prompt: What game were the kids playing under the streetlight?
questions.explanation: Priya deals cards and says "lowest card loses a life," showing they are playing a card game.

questions.prompt: Why could the kids suddenly see so many stars?
choices: It was a clear night in the countryside
The power outage removed the streetlights' glow
questions.explanation: The passage notes the usual "orange haze" from streetlights was gone, letting more stars show — a result of the blackout.

questions.prompt: How does Priya's reaction to the stars compare with Devon's?
choices: She is just as amazed as he is
She is more focused on the game than the sky
She has never seen stars before
She is afraid of the dark
questions.explanation: While Devon is awestruck, Priya glances up briefly and returns her attention to the card game, showing she is more focused on playing.

questions.prompt: In the passage, "unimpressed" most nearly means:
questions.explanation: Priya's quick glance and return to the game shows she was not particularly interested — unimpressed.

questions.prompt: What happened right after the storm, according to the passage?
choices: The kids went inside to sleep
Number seven was the only streetlight left standing
The power came back on immediately
questions.explanation: The passage opens by stating number seven was the only streetlight left standing on Larkin Avenue after the storm.

questions.prompt: Which word in this sentence is an adjective? "The enormous whale surfaced quietly."
questions.explanation: "Enormous" describes the noun "whale," making it an adjective.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: "Neither of the boys ___ ready."
questions.explanation: "Neither" is singular, so it takes the singular verb "is."

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the past perfect tense correctly?
choices: She had finished her homework before dinner.
She finish her homework before dinner.
She finishing her homework before dinner.
She will finished her homework before dinner.
questions.explanation: Past perfect uses "had" + past participle to show an action completed before another past action: "had finished."

questions.prompt: Choose the correct pronoun: "Give the book to Marc and ___."
questions.explanation: As the object of the preposition "to," the correct pronoun is "me," not "I."

questions.prompt: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
choices: Its a beautiful day, isn't it?
It's a beautiful day, isn't it?
Its' a beautiful day, isnt it?
It's a beautiful day, isnt it?
questions.explanation: "It's" is the contraction for "it is," and the tag question needs an apostrophe: "isn't."

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: "___ going to the park after school."
questions.explanation: "They're" is the contraction for "they are," which fits here.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: "Please put the books over ___."
questions.explanation: "There" refers to a place, which fits this sentence.

questions.prompt: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: The correct spelling follows "i before e except after c": receive.

questions.prompt: In the sentence "She quickly closed the door," what part of speech is "quickly"?
questions.explanation: "Quickly" describes how she closed the door, making it an adverb.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is in the future tense?
questions.explanation: "Will walk" indicates an action that has not happened yet — the future tense.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses commas correctly?
choices: I packed pencils pens and a ruler.
I packed pencils, pens, and a ruler.
I packed, pencils pens and a ruler.
I packed pencils pens, and a ruler.
questions.explanation: Items in a series are separated by commas, including before "and" in the Oxford comma style: pencils, pens, and a ruler.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: "The team of scientists ___ presenting their results tomorrow."
questions.explanation: "Team" is a singular collective noun here, so it takes the singular verb "is."

questions.prompt: Which word means the same as "enormous"?
questions.explanation: "Huge" is a synonym for "enormous" — both mean very large.

questions.prompt: Which word is the opposite of "generous"?
questions.explanation: "Stingy" means unwilling to give, the opposite of "generous."

questions.prompt: Puppy is to dog as kitten is to ___.
questions.explanation: A puppy is a baby dog, just as a kitten is a baby cat.

questions.prompt: "The classroom was a zoo" is an example of a:
questions.explanation: A metaphor directly states one thing is another (without "like" or "as"), comparing the classroom to a zoo.

questions.prompt: "Her smile was as bright as the sun" is an example of a:
questions.explanation: A simile compares two things using "like" or "as" — here, "as bright as the sun."

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses personification?
choices: The wind howled through the trees.
questions.explanation: Giving the wind a human ability — "howled" — is personification.

questions.prompt: What does the idiom "it's raining cats and dogs" mean?
choices: Animals are falling from the sky
questions.explanation: This idiom simply means it is raining very hard — it isn't literal.

questions.prompt: Which word means the same as "reluctant"?
questions.explanation: "Reluctant" and "unwilling" both describe hesitation to do something.

questions.prompt: Which word is the opposite of "ancient"?
questions.explanation: "Modern" is the opposite of "ancient," which means very old.

questions.prompt: Author is to book as composer is to ___.
questions.explanation: Just as an author writes a book, a composer writes a song (or piece of music).

questions.prompt: Which word does not belong with the others?
questions.explanation: Trout, salmon, and cod are all fish; a dolphin is a mammal.

questions.prompt: What letter comes next? B, D, F, H, ___
questions.explanation: The pattern skips one letter each time (B, D, F, H), so the next letter is J.

questions.prompt: If CAT is coded as DBU, how is DOG coded using the same rule?
questions.explanation: Each letter shifts forward by one in the alphabet: D→E, O→P, G→H, giving EPH.

questions.prompt: Hot is to cold as up is to ___.
questions.explanation: "Hot" and "cold" are opposites, just as "up" and "down" are opposites.

questions.prompt: Facing north, you turn 90 degrees to your right. Which direction are you facing now?
questions.explanation: Turning 90 degrees right (clockwise) from north points you east.

questions.prompt: Which word does not belong with the others?
questions.explanation: Triangle, square, and circle are 2D shapes; a cube is a 3D shape.

questions.prompt: What comes next? Z, X, V, T, ___
questions.explanation: The pattern moves backward, skipping one letter each time (Z, X, V, T), so the next letter is R.

questions.prompt: You walk 3 blocks north, then 2 blocks east, then 3 blocks south. Which direction must you walk to return to your starting point?
questions.explanation: The north and south walks cancel out, leaving you 2 blocks east of the start, so you must walk west to return.
